description: Irreversibility scores for HTTP methods. Scores are baseline; endpoint context can raise them.

patterns.explanation: Read-only request. Does not modify state.
Metadata-only request. Does not modify state.
Capability discovery request. Does not modify state.
Creates a resource. Usually reversible by deleting the created resource, but may trigger side effects (emails, payments, webhooks).
patterns.safer_alternative: Confirm the endpoint is not a payment, send, or trigger action before allowing.

patterns.explanation: Replaces a resource entirely. Previous state is lost unless backed up.
patterns.safer_alternative: Snapshot the resource before the call so the prior state can be restored.

patterns.explanation: Partially modifies a resource. Overwritten fields are lost unless backed up.
patterns.safer_alternative: Capture the affected fields before the call.

patterns.explanation: Removes a resource. Typically irreversible unless the provider has a trash/recovery window.
patterns.safer_alternative: Require human confirmation. Verify the resource is not production data or a backup.
